note: Shared cases for the routine day-completion rule, read by two tests in two crates that share no Rust code: `roll_up_agrees_with_the_shared_day_fixture` in core/src/routines.rs, and `day_progress_agrees_with_the_shared_day_fixture` in tauri-app/frontend/src/routine_progress.rs. Each side runs the case through its own implementation and must land on the same answer. `item_ids` are the routine's CURRENT items — removed ones are filtered out by the caller on both sides, so a case models post-filter input. `expect.skipped` is asserted by the core side only: the screen renders `done/total` and computes nothing else. Editing an expectation here changes what the app and the assistant both mean by 'done' — that is a product decision, never a tidy-up.

cases.name: every current item has a row
cases.why: the ordinary complete day; without it the fixture only ever tests edges

cases.name: a skipped item still counts the day complete
cases.why: user decision 2026-09-08 — a skip is a deliberate act with a reason attached, so a morning where one item was skipped on purpose is a morning that happened

cases.name: a day of nothing but skips is still complete
cases.why: the decision taken to its limit — and the day whose `skipped` count is the whole story

cases.name: an item with no row leaves the day incomplete
cases.why: untouched is not skipped; only a row of either kind counts

cases.name: two rows for one item is one item done, not two
cases.why: an undo-then-skip writes a second row; counting rows instead of items would report a complete day off one item

cases.name: a row for an item no longer in the routine is ignored
cases.why: otherwise a deleted item's history would keep old days looking complete, or count toward new ones

cases.name: rows from a neighbouring day do not count toward this one
cases.why: core groups by date while the screen is handed one date's rows; both must land on the same day boundary

cases.name: a day with no rows at all
cases.why: core omits such a day from its output entirely while the screen still draws it as 0-of-N; absence and a zero row must mean the same thing

cases.name: a routine with no items is never complete
cases.why: an empty routine would otherwise report a perfect streak forever, every item of nothing being done
